## copilotkitCustomizeConfig

Customize the LangGraph configuration for use in CopilotKit.

To install the CopilotKit SDK, run:

```bash
npm install @copilotkit/sdk-js @langchain/langgraph @langchain/core@1.3.7 langchain@1.6.4 zod@^3.25
```

`@copilotkit/sdk-js` needs zod 3. `@langchain/core` 1.4 and later, and `langchain` 1.6.5 and later, need zod 4, so `npm install @copilotkit/sdk-js` alone fails with `ERESOLVE`. The pinned versions accept zod 3.

### Examples

Disable emitting messages and tool calls:

```typescript
import { copilotkitCustomizeConfig } from "@copilotkit/sdk-js/langgraph";

const customConfig = copilotkitCustomizeConfig(config, {
  emitMessages: false,
  emitToolCalls: false,
});
```

To emit a tool call as streaming LangGraph state, pass the destination key in state,
the tool name and optionally the tool argument. (If you don't pass the argument name,
all arguments are emitted under the state key.)

```typescript
import { copilotkitCustomizeConfig } from "@copilotkit/sdk-js/langgraph";

const customConfig = copilotkitCustomizeConfig(config, {
  emitIntermediateState: [
    {
      stateKey: "steps",
      tool: "SearchTool",
      toolArgument: "steps",
    },
  ],
});
```

### Parameters

<PropertyReference name="baseConfig" type="RunnableConfig" required > 
The LangChain/LangGraph configuration to customize.
</PropertyReference>

<PropertyReference name="options" type="OptionsConfig"  > 
Configuration options.

  <PropertyReference name="emitMessages" type="boolean" default="true">
    Emit messages to CopilotKit. Pass `false` to stop emitting messages.
  </PropertyReference>

  <PropertyReference name="emitToolCalls" type="boolean | string | string[]" default="true">
    Emit tool calls to CopilotKit. Pass `false` to stop emitting tool calls. Pass a tool name or a list of tool names to emit only those tool calls.
  </PropertyReference>

  <PropertyReference name="emitAll" type="boolean">
    Emit all messages and tool calls. When `true`, `emitMessages` and `emitToolCalls` are ignored.
  </PropertyReference>

  <PropertyReference name="emitIntermediateState" type="IntermediateStateConfig[]">
    Emit tool calls as streaming LangGraph state. Each entry takes `stateKey`, `tool`, and an optional `toolArgument`.
  </PropertyReference>
</PropertyReference>

## copilotkitExit

Exits the current agent after the run completes. Calling copilotkitExit() will
not immediately stop the agent. Instead, it signals to CopilotKit to stop the agent after
the run completes.

### Examples

```typescript
import type { RunnableConfig } from "@langchain/core/runnables";
import { copilotkitExit } from "@copilotkit/sdk-js/langgraph";

async function myNode(state: AgentState, config: RunnableConfig) {
  await copilotkitExit(config);
  return state;
}
```

### Parameters

<PropertyReference name="config" type="RunnableConfig" required > 
The LangChain/LangGraph configuration.
</PropertyReference>

## copilotkitEmitState

Emits intermediate state to CopilotKit. Useful if you have a longer running node and you want to
update the user with the current state of the node.

### Examples

```typescript
import { copilotkitEmitState } from "@copilotkit/sdk-js/langgraph";

for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
  await someLongRunningOperation(i);
  await copilotkitEmitState(config, { progress: i });
}
```

### Parameters

<PropertyReference name="config" type="RunnableConfig" required > 
The LangChain/LangGraph configuration.
</PropertyReference>

<PropertyReference name="state" type="any" required > 
The state to emit.
</PropertyReference>

## copilotkitEmitMessage

Manually emits a message to CopilotKit. Useful in longer running nodes to update the user.
Important: You still need to return the messages from the node.

### Examples

```typescript
import { AIMessage } from "@langchain/core/messages";
import { copilotkitEmitMessage } from "@copilotkit/sdk-js/langgraph";

const message = "Step 1 of 10 complete";
await copilotkitEmitMessage(config, message);

// Return the message from the node
return {
  messages: [new AIMessage({ content: message })],
};
```

### Parameters

<PropertyReference name="config" type="RunnableConfig" required > 
The LangChain/LangGraph configuration.
</PropertyReference>

<PropertyReference name="message" type="string" required > 
The message to emit.
</PropertyReference>

## copilotkitEmitToolCall

Manually emits a tool call to CopilotKit.

### Examples

```typescript
import { copilotkitEmitToolCall } from "@copilotkit/sdk-js/langgraph";

const autoId = await copilotkitEmitToolCall(config, "SearchTool", { steps: 10 });

// With a custom ID for correlation/idempotency:
const customId = await copilotkitEmitToolCall(config, "SearchTool", { steps: 10 }, { toolCallId: "my-custom-id" });
```

### Parameters

<PropertyReference name="config" type="RunnableConfig" required > 
The LangChain/LangGraph configuration.
</PropertyReference>

<PropertyReference name="name" type="string" required > 
The name of the tool to emit.
</PropertyReference>

<PropertyReference name="args" type="any" required > 
The arguments to emit.
</PropertyReference>

<PropertyReference name="options" type="{ toolCallId?: string; }"  > 
Options for the tool call emission.
</PropertyReference>

### Returns

The tool call ID used for the emitted call. It equals `options.toolCallId`
when provided, otherwise a randomly generated ID.

## copilotKitInterrupt

Pauses the graph with a LangGraph interrupt and shows a message or a tool call to the user in CopilotKit. Pass `message` or `action`.

<Callout type="warn" title="Use LangGraph's interrupt() for now">
  In `@copilotkit/sdk-js` 1.89.0, `copilotKitInterrupt` fails the run with a `CopilotKitMisuseError` ("Failed to create interrupt") instead of pausing the graph. Call `interrupt()` from `@langchain/langgraph` in your node, and handle it in the frontend with [`useInterrupt`](/human-in-the-loop/useInterrupt). The graph needs a checkpointer.

  ```typescript
  import { interrupt } from "@langchain/langgraph";

  async function approvalNode(state: AgentState) {
    // Pauses the run. Returns the value the frontend resumes with.
    const answer = interrupt("Do you approve this plan?");
    return { approved: answer };
  }
  ```
</Callout>

### Parameters

<PropertyReference name="message" type="string">
  Text to show the user. Pass `message` or `action`. One of them is required.
</PropertyReference>

<PropertyReference name="action" type="string">
  Name of the tool call to send to the frontend. Used when you do not pass `message`.
</PropertyReference>

<PropertyReference name="args" type="Record<string, any>" default="{}">
  Arguments for the `action` tool call.
</PropertyReference>

### Returns

`{ answer, messages }`. `messages` is the resume value, and `answer` is the `content` of its last message.

## convertActionsToDynamicStructuredTools

Converts the frontend actions that CopilotKit puts in `state.copilotkit.actions` into LangChain `DynamicStructuredTool` objects. Bind them to your model so it can call your frontend tools.

### Examples

```typescript
import { convertActionsToDynamicStructuredTools } from "@copilotkit/sdk-js/langgraph";

const modelWithTools = model.bindTools([
  ...convertActionsToDynamicStructuredTools(state.copilotkit?.actions ?? []),
  ...tools,
]);
```

### Parameters

<PropertyReference name="actions" type="any[]" required>
  The actions to convert. Each entry is an action, or an object `{ type: "function", function: action }`. Each action needs `name`, `description`, and `parameters` (a JSON Schema).
</PropertyReference>

### Returns

A `DynamicStructuredTool[]`, one tool per action. The tools do not run anything on the agent side. The frontend runs the tool call.

To convert one action, use `convertActionToDynamicStructuredTool(action)`. It takes the same action shape and returns one `DynamicStructuredTool`.
